reviewer: Codex, independent; did not author the subject
reviewScope: SATISFIED-GRADE review of exact-byte fixture authoring only. This verdict does not mark DR-103 SATISFIED, does not close DR-120 or ID-DEP-8, and does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/.
summary: Byte custody is intact, but required fixture classes are missing, malformed, or undecidable from their retained bytes. The corpus is not SATISFIED-grade.

blockers.title: The mandatory V2-A1 schema successor has not landed
blockers.detail: The live DR-103 row requires V2-A1's defining sentence to land in a successor edit before, or in the same act as, fixture generation. This corpus still binds component-manifest-schemas.v2 at 73114dde..., whose entryShape says stableId is unique among LIVE entries and whose RJ-2 collision universe has no same-stableId exclusion. TC-ACCEPT.index-multiversion and TC-ACCEPT.index-all-accept nevertheless carry two LIVE entries with the same stableId/name/root and declare ACCEPT. Under the corpus's bound schema those outcomes remain textually contradictory, so the ordering requirement and the expected outcome both fail.
blockers.requiredRepair: Land and independently review the required schema successor, then author and repin the corpus against that successor. Do not infer the missing exclusion from fixture intent.

blockers.title: TC-ACCEPT.maximal does not populate every designed field
blockers.detail: The required class is a maximal manifest with every designed field populated. The fixture leaves capabilities empty, omits configuration, omits commands[].args, and omits options[].default. These are active designed shapes, not reserved binding points. The file is a valid-looking expanded manifest, but it is not the required maximal member.
blockers.requiredRepair: Populate every applicable active field and nested field, retain all referenced bytes, and repin every dependent index and lock.

blockers.title: The ACCEPT lock outcomes are prohibited while DR-111 is open
blockers.detail: Both TC-ACCEPT lock fixtures contain resolutionInputs.request[].versionConstraint and are declared ACCEPT. ID-DEP-4 states that until DR-111 closes, no lock over a constrained request is producible at all. The live register still marks DR-111 OPEN. The multi-component lock does structurally list maximal plus its minimal dependency, but its ACCEPT outcome is not currently decidable under the bound schema.
blockers.requiredRepair: Do not state unconditional ACCEPT until the version-constraint surface closes or a reviewed successor provides a presently decidable lock-input shape.

blockers.title: Required TC-NAME members are absent or do not exercise the claimed rule
blockers.detail: There is no reserved-alias-form fixture, no parent-linkage-collision fixture, and no clean alias-vs-alias collision fixture. TC-NAME.id-version-not-distinct puts a UUID into the semver field; that is structural invalidity, not the required case where a version datum is used as an identity key. In addition, most RJ-2 fixtures record only the family RJ-2 rather than the exact subcode required by the corpus discipline. The alias-cycle bytes also shadow two live command names, and the multiple-roots bytes also create a root-name mismatch, leaving their claimed single subcodes non-unique.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add one decidable, digest-pinned fixture for every named member and give each RJ-2 fixture one exact expected subcode without an earlier or competing failure.

blockers.title: Context-dependent TC-NAME outcomes lack the custody needed to decide them
blockers.detail: TC-NAME.reserved-root, live-name-collision, alias-collision, and hostile-double-mount are standalone manifests with no index/reserved-list packet; absent that live custody, several are valid standalone manifests. The parity packet merely repeats two hand-authored equal arrays and carries no live-host-grammar source or digest, so it cannot be a live-grammar CI parity fixture. The stale-alias packets carry an asOf date but no as-of host-core release observation, so the release-cycle half of the dual clock cannot be independently recomputed, especially for the claimed after-window non-resolution.
blockers.requiredRepair: Packet each contextual case with the exact index/reserved/live-grammar/release-clock bytes or digest-pinned observations needed to compute the outcome.

blockers.title: The TC-CLOSURE packets do not instantiate the three required failures
blockers.detail: TC-CLOSURE.undeclared-edge requests two roots while its manifest declares no dependencies; two explicit roots do not establish an undeclared dependency edge discovered during closure. TC-CLOSURE.absent-stableId has no manifest whose declared closure references the absent ID and no index bytes, only informal request/indexContains fields. TC-CLOSURE.implicit-download is prose describing an attempt and an expected remediation; it carries no manifest, index, attempted acquisition datum, or typed remediation record. These members are named, not runnable or schema-decidable fixtures.
blockers.requiredRepair: Author actual manifest/index/request packets that force each RJ-5 trigger and carry a concrete typed-remediation expectation for the implicit-download case.

blockers.title: The metadata-only probe contains no executable recorder
blockers.detail: The required probe needs an executable that records execution and a recorder whose retained state can show zero executions after admission/discovery/help/completion/inventory. The only claimed executable is dummy.onebyte: one read-only byte 0x78 ('x'), with no executable format and no recorder/state path. recordsExecution:true is an assertion, not authored probe behavior.
blockers.requiredRepair: Provide a runnable, platform-appropriate execution-recording fixture plus digest-pinned initial/final recorder custody and an invocation contract for all five operations.

blockers.title: TC-SIG.lock-artifact-digest-mismatch has no artifact bytes to mismatch
blockers.detail: The lock contains invented 11..., 22..., and 33... digests but references no retained index, manifest, or artifact bytes. None of those three digests identifies any authored[] or supportingBytes[] member. A checker cannot distinguish DIGEST_MISMATCH from missing custody, so the required artifact-bytes-versus-lock-digest class is only labeled.
blockers.requiredRepair: Retain and reference the actual artifact bytes and use a recorded lock digest that differs from their recomputed SHA-256.

blockers.title: ACCEPT index custody does not retain or identify detached envelope bytes
blockers.detail: Every ACCEPT index entry carries a truncated value such as sig:6f8203ff7b15b316, while the schema defines the envelope identity as the SHA-256 of envelope bytes. No detached envelope appears in authored[] or supportingBytes[], and TC-ACCEPT.index-multiversion reuses the same signatureRef for two different manifest digests. This review does not demand DR-112 ceremony semantics, but exact-byte identity and association still must be recomputable for an ACCEPT custody record.
blockers.requiredRepair: Retain each detached envelope's exact bytes and full SHA-256 identity, associate it unambiguously with its manifest, and repin dependent indexes and locks without asserting ceremony validity.

shouldFix.title: Eight single-path TC-PATH fixtures are masked by ENTRYPOINT_ABSENT
shouldFix.detail: dotdot, dot, absolute, backslash, drive-letter, nul, empty-segment, and non-nfc replace the committed bin/entry path but leave platforms[0].entrypoint equal to bin/entry. Each therefore also triggers the separate entrypoint-absent rule, allowing an implementation that omits the intended path check to pass through the fallback RJ-3 trigger. Keep the entrypoint matched to the deliberately malformed path, or otherwise isolate the intended rule.
